newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australian dlr regains ground as yen retreats.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australian dlr regains ground as yen retreats.

text.p: The Australian dollar drifted to a firmer finish Monday as a steady flow of funds out of the yen helped rescue it from an unpromising start.

The currency had been threatening US$0.7950 support after recoiling from the 80 cent barrier last week but a bout of yen selling and a chunky single order for AUD/NZD forced a bear squeeze in a painfully thin market.

That saw it recover US$0.7970 resistance where it stayed for much of a sleepy session despite a couple of discordant quotes down at US$0.7935 late in the day. Dealers felt the bounce meant the US$0.7950/8000 range should hold until new year.
By 5.00 pm (0600 GMT) the local dollar had managed a shallow bounce to US$0.7965/70 from an opening US$0.7952/57 and US$0.7961/66 late here on Friday.

The recapture of US$0.7970 resistance repaired some of the technical damage by last week's failure at 80 cents but dealers doubted the momentum was there to re-try that level with the New Year holiday so near.

On the crosses it climbed to 92.40/50 yen, its best finish in almost a month, from an early 91.87/97 and 91.50/60 late Friday. In trade weighted terms it nudged up to 59.4 from a previous 59.3 finish.

The Japanese currency came under pressure as Tokyo stocks extended their recent decline in the morning session, so reinforcing the perception that interest rates there will be staying at record lows for some time to come.

Stocks later recovered almost all their losses today but the Nikkei was still down over 1,600 points, or eight percent, on the month. That contrasted with the strength of U.S. stocks, which hit another record high Friday, where booming asset prices could just tip the Federal Reserve into tightening next year.
The U.S. dollar benefited as a result and in late trade was testing 3-1/2 year highs at 116.05/10 yen.

The percepion that Japanese rates were not heading higher offered bulls hope that Japanese investors would continue to pump funds into the AUD even though it was less of a higher yielder following the Reserve Bank's surprise 0.5 point rate cut of December 11.

But there was still a risk domestic rates would be eased yet again in the new year if Q4 inflation and wages data due in February proved subdued and jobs growth showed no signs of picking up. While that danger existed, analysts felt it would be hard for the longer term uptrend to resume and trouble the early December peak of US$0.8212. -- Wayne Cole 61-2 9373 1800
